visualReview.notes: Inspected 11 current portable/source-terrain frames. Liège Saint-Paul Cathedral has an individually authored Gothic nave,projecting north/south transept gables and faceted eastern choir,steep gray slate roofs,stepped buttresses/flying struts,pinnacles and recessed tall pointed glazing. Simple cream mullions/foils/transoms and three blind gable panels approximate visible Gothic detail. Western square paired-louver tower has corner turrets,clocks attached to its sloping lower spire,a genuinely open upper lantern and long final point. Low slate cloister ranges,selected dormers and round stair turret surround a genuinely open garth. Corrected cornices floating outside the upper nave,detached clock disks,windows intersected by buttresses/flying struts,and a cloister recess blocked by overlapping walls. Fine carving,exact stained-glass artwork,hidden bays and full interiors are simplified or excluded.
